title: A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks
author: E.F. Codd (1970)
description: Codd's seminal paper introducing the relational model for databases, establishing concepts like relations, domains, keys, and normalization that revolutionized modern database design.

title: Attention Is All You Need
author: Vaswani et al. (2017)
description: The groundbreaking paper that introduced the Transformer architecture, replacing recurrent and convolutional networks with self-attention and forming the foundation of modern Large Language Models.

title: The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine
author: Brin & Page (1998)
description: The original paper by Google's founders describing the architecture of their prototype search engine, introducing the PageRank algorithm and early web indexing structures.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
author: He et al. (2015)
description: Introduced the ResNet architecture and residual connections, enabling the training of extremely deep neural networks by resolving the vanishing gradient problem.

title: The Rigged Monopoly Game: Observer's Attributions and Reactions to Unequal Allocation of Resources
author: Nitert, M. G. (2022)
description: This study examines how observers perceive and react to unequal resource allocation through the lens of a rigged Monopoly game, providing insights into attitudes towards economic inequality and resource distribution.

title: The Economics of Healthcare Rationing
author: Michael Frakes, Matthew Frank, Kyle Rozema (2015)
description: This comprehensive analysis examines the economics of healthcare rationing decisions, including cost-benefit and cost-effectiveness analysis. The paper explores how economic analyses inform healthcare coverage decisions and discusses practical and conceptual challenges that span both economics and ethics in healthcare resource allocation.

title: The Google File System
author: Sanjay Ghemawat, Howard Gobioff, and Shun-Tak Leung (2003)
description: Describes GFS, a scalable distributed file system designed for data-intensive applications, emphasizing fault tolerance, high throughput, and running on commodity hardware.

title: MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters
author: Jeffrey Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat (2004)
description: Google's classic paper defining MapReduce, a programming model and implementation for processing large-scale datasets in a parallel, distributed manner on large commodity clusters.

title: Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data
author: Fay Chang, Jeffrey Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Wilson C. Hsieh, Deborah A. Wallach, Mike Burrows, Tushar Chandra, Andrew Fikes, and Robert E. Gruber (2006)
description: Outlines Bigtable, Google's proprietary wide-column distributed storage system designed to scale to petabytes of structured data across thousands of commodity servers.

title: Dynamo: Amazon’s Highly Available Key-value Store
author: Giuseppe DeCandia, Deniz Hastorun, Madan Jampani, Gunavardhan Kakulapati, Avinash Lakshman, Alex Pilchin, Swaminathan Sivasubramanian, Peter Vosshall, and Werner Vogels (2007)
description: Details Dynamo, Amazon's highly available, decentralized key-value storage system utilizing consistent hashing and eventual consistency to achieve masterless replication.

title: Dremel: Interactive Analysis of Web-Scale Datasets
author: Sergey Melnik, Andrey Gubarev, Jing Jing Long, Geoffrey Romer, Shiva Shivakumar, Matt Tolton, and Theo Vassilakis (2010)
description: Describes Dremel, Google's query engine for nested structured data, combining columnar storage and multi-level execution trees to run SQL queries on petabytes in seconds.

title: Resilient Distributed Datasets: A Fault-Tolerant Abstraction for In-Memory Cluster Computing
author: Matei Zaharia, Mosharaf Chowdhury, Michael J. Franklin, Scott Shenker, and Ion Stoica (2012)
description: Introduces RDDs, the core abstraction behind Apache Spark, allowing fault-tolerant, in-memory computations on large clusters for high-performance iterative algorithms.

title: What You See Is What It Does: A Structural Pattern for Legible Software
author: Eagon Meng & Daniel Jackson (2025)
description: Explores architectural design patterns in modern software systems that align system internals with user perception, enhancing legibility, usability, and maintainability.

title: Data Structures for Statistical Computing in Python
author: Wes McKinney (2010)
description: The classic paper introducing the pandas library to the scientific Python community, detailing the design of high-performance DataFrame data structures for analysis.

title: Python for Data Analysis (2nd ed.)
author: Wes McKinney (2017)
description: A comprehensive handbook by pandas creator Wes McKinney, detailing essential techniques for data manipulation, cleaning, exploratory analysis, and visualization in Python.

title: pandas (project)
author: pandas-dev (orig. Wes McKinney)
description: The open-source project documentation and repository home for pandas, the foundational data analysis and manipulation library for the Python programming language.

title: A Programmable Dual-RNA–Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
author: Jinek et al. (2012)
description: The landmark study demonstrating that the CRISPR/Cas9 system can be programmed to cut specific DNA sequences, laying the foundation for modern gene editing.

title: MDPI IJMS CRISPR/Cas9 Delivery Systems to Enhance Gene Editing EfficiencyArticle (Vol. 26, No. 9, 4420)
description: A comprehensive scientific review highlighting advanced delivery vehicles (both viral and non-viral) designed to improve CRISPR/Cas9 target efficiency and specificity.
